headline: INR 795 Cr revenue - and paid clicks land on a store-locator. That single step is the leak.
ad_intro: Licious runs one of the largest paid footprints we have audited in Indian food D2C: ~300 live Google Ads creatives under Delightful Gourmet Pvt Ltd, plus a Meta presence we verified live (Library ID 983369480870934, running since 15 Apr 2026). The product story is excellent - 'caught in small boats', 'never frozen', '0-4C from source to store'. The gap is where the money lands: the live Bengaluru Meta ad routes traffic to licious.in/store-locator, and Google spend is spread across a very wide creative base - while FY25 closed at INR 795 Cr revenue with a INR 218.3 Cr net loss. The three fixes below make the existing spend convert harder; they do not ask for a bigger budget.
ad_intelligence: ~300 live creatives under Delightful Gourmet Pvt Ltd - brand, category and Local store ads (we captured e.g. 'Licious Neo Town Electronic City' store-level ads).
Active ads confirmed in Meta Ad Library - Library ID 983369480870934, first seen 15 Apr 2026. This is a sustained flight, not a test.

Cold-chain trust stack: 'Your favourite Fish & Seafood', 'Caught in small boats', 'No added chemicals', 'Never frozen', 'Maintained at 0-4C from source to store' - plus a Kannada-language hook for Bengaluru.
licious.in/store-locator?city_name=Bengaluru&city_id=1 - the click lands on a city/store picker, one full step before any product or price.
FY25 revenue INR 795 Cr, net loss INR 218.3 Cr; ~USD 490M raised; IPO reportedly deferred to FY27-28. Efficiency is the board-level conversation right now.
findings: Destination leak (highest cost): the verified live Meta ad for Bengaluru sends clicks to the store-locator. Every extra step between ad and cart costs conversion - and this is the single most expensive step you can add to a food ad, because freshness intent decays in seconds. Fix: deep-link to the SKU page with city pre-selected, keep the locator as a secondary link.

Spend spread: ~300 creatives including a large agency-run Local store-ad layer (Freeflow is not the buyer here - Delightful Gourmet is the verified advertiser). With this volume, budget is being thinned across many assets and geos instead of concentrated on the SKU/geo clusters that carry the cold-chain promise best.
Promise not carried into the landing: 'Never frozen' and '0-4C' are your strongest assets - they should be the hero of the destination page, not just the ad. The locator page does not carry them.

Measurement risk: with Meta + Google + Local store ads running together, if CAPI / Enhanced Conversions are not clean, Smart Bidding optimises on partial signal - you pay more per order without a visible reason.
competitors: Category landing pages with same-day delivery proof above the fold.
Deep-link ad traffic to category pages (fish / chicken / mutton) with delivery-slot proof, not a locator.
Subscription-first funnel; retention mechanics pull users back weekly.
Licious already offers subscription - surface it inside the ad landing path and in retargeting.
Set a 10-minute delivery expectation inside the app.
Do not fight on speed. Win on cold-chain trust and source story - make that the landing hero.
wins: WIN 1 - CRO: Route meta clicks to the product page, not the locator
Rewrite the 5 highest-spend Bengaluru Meta ads to land on the SKU page with city_id=1 pre-set and the locator as a secondary CTA. Keep UTMs identical so the comparison stays clean for 14 days.
WIN 2 - Creative: Systemise the cold-chain proof

Take the assets that already work ('small boats', 'never frozen') and build a repeatable 3-format system: 15s cold-chain proof Reel, 15s source-story Reel, 15s offer card. Refresh weekly from one shoot day instead of ad-hoc creatives.
WIN 3 - Tracking: Meta CAPI + Enhanced Conversions
Audit server-side events end to end, dedupe browser/server, and pass order value. If Smart Bidding sees full signal, the same spend buys more carts - before any creative change.
